name: hay-rack-charming

purpose.role_in_scene: animals eat from it; fill level changes
purpose.why: Rebuilt on Evan's request (2026-10-22) to replace the Ranch tile's original model with a crafted one, keeping its game role.
purpose.audience: children building and playing in a miniature ranch

brief.prompt: a whimsical storybook version of a wooden slatted hay feeder rack on four legs, V-shaped slats, filled with golden hay, chunky rounded toy-like proportions, bulging and plump

concept.tool: Midjourney web app (midjourney.com/imagine), driven in Evan's signed-in Chrome by Claude through the Claude in Chrome extension, one job at a time, text prompts only (no image reference)

hero.prompt: a whimsical storybook version of a wooden slatted hay feeder rack on four legs, V-shaped slats, filled with golden hay, chunky rounded toy-like proportions, bulging and plump, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 1:1
hero.pick_reason: plump V-slatted rack on four legs heaped with hay, clearest V slats

turnaround.prompt: orthographic turnaround sheet, front view, side view, back view, evenly spaced, same scale, a whimsical storybook version of a wooden slatted hay feeder rack on four legs, V-shaped slats, filled with golden hay, chunky rounded toy-like proportions, bulging and plump, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 16:9
turnaround.pick_reason: front, three-quarter and end view of one slatted rack with hay, evenly spaced

construction.by: modeler agent, directed by the art director (Claude)

rounds.change: First charming build from the normal build.py: box crib with flared walls, rims, posts, caps, splayed legs, 5/3 slats in \ / pairs, sphere-mapped hay pillow with 26 tufts. Camera calibrated to -48/16.
Rims, posts, legs and slats made much fatter (6/4 slats), legs shorter splay, hay lower and wider, tufts flattened outward over the rim.
Taller walls and darker timber/hay colours to the hero's tone.
Crib lowered (rims 0.85 / 0.34 m), hay to 1.10 m; camera recalibrated to -50/16.
Beams turned into cheap rounded logs (bevel only along the length) to get under 2k triangles; 7/5 wider slats; less hay bulge.
Varied slat lean instead of a WWW zigzag, fuller hay cushion, 10 tufts, more lean on the crib; hay kept inside the slats, thinner streaks, rounder dome.
Hay height tried at 1.17 m (0.865) and settled at 1.12 m; partial raised to 0.84 m so it reads; thinner twine bands on the carried sheaf.
Final 768 px / 48 samples: slats narrowed to 6/4 at 0.105 m so they read as separate boards with gaps like the hero (IoU cost 0.003, worth it).

what_was_done: Copied models/hay-rack (build.py, make_views.py, hero_check.py, run.sh) and reshaped it. Same states (full, partial, empty, carried), same origin (footprint centre on the ground), long side at the front (-Y), same material names and roles (Timber_Pine, Hay_Gold, Hay_Light) and object names (frame, slats, hay, straw_gold, straw_light). Footprint 1.37 x 1.06 m against the normal 1.36 x 1.06 m, so it drops in at the same width/depth ratio.

The hero wins. It drew a chubby box crib, not the normal rack's V, so the V survives as walls that flare out to the top. views/hero.png is the MJ hero keyed on B/G < 0.60; the mask also kept the warm cast shadow under the crib, so below the lower rim only hand-traced leg polygons are kept (the potting-bench method). The sheet's left cut (a straight-on long side) is scored as views/view_front.png for reference only: the sheet's crib is taller and boxier, with straight walls and straight legs. Its 3/4 middle view and the second long side are dropped.

The charming hero sees the -X end on the left and the long front on the right, so hero_check.py sits off the front-left corner: 50 deg off the front towards -X, 16 deg up, orthographic (calibrated over a yaw/elevation grid).

Timber_Pine. A fat top rim (0.15 x 0.16 m logs) and a fat lower rim (0.14 m), each four beams crossing at the corners with log ends 8 cm past each other, long beams a hair above the end beams like notched logs. Logs are rounded only along their length (two bevel segments on the four long edges, flat-cut ends) to stay in budget. Corner posts (0.13 m) with knobbly rotated caps, chunky slats (6 per long wall, 4 per end, 0.105 m) leaning in a mix of directions, three floor boards on the lower rim, and four stubby 0.14 m legs splayed out under the corners.

Everything is fatter and rounder than the normal rack (rims 2x the normal rail section, legs 1.6x), the top rim sits 3 cm off the lower one so the whole crib leans a little, slats wobble a couple of degrees each, and caps are set askew.

Hay_Gold pillow: a squashed sphere mapped into the flared crib (just inside the slats) with a rounded cushion dome over the rim, lumpy, then 10 fat tufts (wide 2-tri cards, mostly lying outward over the rim) and 34 thin flat Hay_Light streaks lying on the dome for the hero's combed straw. A few tufts poke out between the slats.

full = the hero pillow (also hay-rack-charming.glb), dome top 1.12 m. partial = a lower pillow ending just under the rim (0.84 m) with fewer tufts. empty = the bare crib with 14 flat strands on the floor boards and 5 caught in the slats. carried = a plump waisted sheaf (0.5 x 0.34 x 0.3 m body, straw bursting from both ends) cinched by two twine bands, resting on the ground at the origin. The bands are a new material, Rope_Twine (fiber role), used only there.
Flat colours, one material per object, no animation (export_animations=False). Triangles: full 1540, partial 1458, empty 1194, carried 440 (budget 2k).
construction.creative_additions: Knobbly askew corner caps, notched log ends, the crib's gentle lean, and twine bands on the carried sheaf.

geometry.up: Z (Blender source); Y in GLB and game
geometry.origin: centre of the footprint, on the ground

good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.862 at 768 px / 48 samples from the calibrated hero camera (best during the rounds 0.882 at 384 px).
Reads small as a chunky toy crib with a gold cushion: fat double rims with log ends, corner caps and stubby splayed legs carry the silhouette.
Same footprint ratio as the normal rack, so the game's rescale keeps it in place; the fill levels read from above.
off: The hero crib is nearly square in plan (its two visible faces are about equal); this one keeps the normal rack's 1.3:1 footprint for the game, so the hero's left end comes out narrower.
The hero's slats are mostly upright with a few diagonals; here they lean in a varied mix and the gaps read darker, with less hay showing through them.
The hero's hay is a dense combed mass; within 2k triangles it is a faceted dome with tufts and flat streaks, spikier up close.
Sheet front view scores 0.611 (reference only): the sheet drew a taller, straight-walled crib.
No wood grain or painted log rings: flat colours only, per the game rules.

rights: Original work for Abbie's World. Concept art generated on Evan's Midjourney account; geometry generated procedurally, no third-party meshes or textures.
